problem: VLM-based VLN policies are trained by observation-to-action prediction, which discards the rich supervision already in each demonstration (which landmark the instruction refers to, its appearance and 3D layout in future frames). Adapting to new routes and instructions is therefore demonstration-hungry. Prior future-prediction methods spend generative rollouts at inference and only fit discrete candidate scoring.
motivation: Demonstrations are expensive, so extracting more supervision per trajectory matters for data-efficient VLN. Navigation is landmark-oriented, so only the instruction-relevant future region should be informative, not the whole future scene. Future frames can therefore act as a training-time teacher and be dropped at deployment.
key_idea: Attach auxiliary explicit ordered-landmark tokens (regressing frozen semantic and VGGT geometric features of the future landmark region) and an implicit token (contrasted against same-scene world-model counterfactuals) to an unmodified VLN backbone, used only during training.
insight: Future supervision helps most when the data is scarce: gains grow from +2.6 SR at 100% to +6.8 at 70% and +5.2 at 30% for InternVLA-N1. Ablations show correctness of the target is critical (a shuffled-future placebo drops SR to 34.9 from a 38.5 baseline), the semantic and geometric targets are complementary, and the number of slots matters (S=10 is best over 2 and 18). The two branches are sub-additive (5.9 explicit and 3.0 implicit vs 6.8 combined at 70%), and world-model negatives add +2.0 SR over cross-environment negatives.
method: Ordered landmark tokens: an LLM parses the instruction offline into at most M ordered landmark phrases filling S=10 slots. Each slot is initialised as a frozen text embedding plus a learned rank embedding, or an empty-slot token.
Object-aware encoder (OAE): cross-attention plus an FFN grounds the slot queries in the current visual tokens together with a Grounding-DINO location token.

Semantic–geometric decoder (SGAD): a lightweight Transformer decoder predicts, for patches of the future landmark box at t+k (k=10), the backbone's frozen patch features and frozen VGGT geometry features. A masked MSE loss with weight β balances the two.

Implicit future token: a learnable query pools frozen visual features, and after the VLM a projector maps the token to a contrastive space. It is pulled toward the pooled future-landmark embedding by InfoNCE.

Same-scene counterfactual negatives: a frozen NanoWM world model, fine-tuned on R2R-CE train, rolls out 10 steps with the last 2 actions heading-flipped. Post-divergence frames serve as hard negatives, added only in stage 2 alongside cross-episode negatives.

Token isolation mask and two-phase loss: attention between explicit and implicit tokens is blocked. The loss weights (w_a,w_e,w_i) are (0.3,1,1) in the first half of training and (1,0.3,0.3) in the second.

Inference: the detector, SGAD, VGGT, projector and world model are discarded. Only the extra tokens remain, and the original action head is unchanged (discrete for NaVILA, diffusion trajectory for InternVLA-N1).

setting.backbone: InternVLA-N1 DualVLN (fine-tuned with FINE) and NaVILA (fine-tuned with FINE)
setting.model_size: about 8B backbone; FINE adds about 143M parameters (about 1.7%)
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrations only, with 100/70/30% nested subsets (R2R 10,819/7,573/3,245 episodes). Frozen Grounding-DINO, VGGT and NanoWM (fine-tuned on R2R-CE train) provide supervision; no extra human annotation or external demonstrations.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (history plus current frame)
setting.action_space: backbone-native: discrete low-level actions (NaVILA) or continuous trajectory chunks via diffusion (InternVLA-N1)
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE on Matterport3D) plus a real humanoid
setting.privileged: none at test time (future frames, detector, VGGT and world model are training-only)

numbers.evidence: Table sota, VLN-CE R2R and RxR val-unseen at 100% training data

numbers_note: NaVILA + FINE at 70% (SR 41.7, SPL 35.5) and 30% (SR 11.9, SPL 10.3) are also in Table dataeff. Real-robot results (Table realworld, 20 trials per setting) are not included as benchmark numbers.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, FINE raises InternVLA-N1 from 58.2 to 60.8 SR at full data and from 38.5 to 45.3 SR at 70%, recovering about a third of the 19.7-point loss. On RxR-CE it adds 4.5 SR (53.5 to 58.0) and is best on most metrics, though JanusVLN† (which uses about 10.7M external pairs) keeps the higher R2R SPL of 56.8. On the real humanoid, InternVLA-N1 + FINE reaches 60% versus 30% SR in the occluded-landmark experiment.
limitations: Requires instructions that decompose into ordered, detectable landmarks that appear in future frames; otherwise the loss is skipped.
Depends on frozen auxiliary models (Grounding-DINO, VGGT, NanoWM), which add training overhead and bound supervision quality.
The reduced-data study subsamples demonstrations within fixed scenes, so it does not measure scene diversity; reduced budgets also get fewer optimizer updates.
